The Florida sun beats down on Sebring, baking the asphalt and making life incredibly difficult for the drivers in these long stints.
You can feel the history here at Sebring, a track that's seen it all, from endurance racing legends to up-and-coming stars battling it out on this iconic circuit.
The smell of racing fuel and burning rubber fills the air, a sensory overload that defines the Sebring experience.
The grandstands are packed with passionate fans, eager to witness another chapter in Sebring's rich motorsport history.
The bumpy surface of Sebring is legendary, a real test of man and machine as they navigate this unforgiving track.
The shadows are starting to lengthen across the circuit as we head towards the later stages of the race, a crucial time for strategy.
Even from the commentary box you can see the heat radiating off the track, tire management will be absolutely key today.
The energy here is electric. Sebring is more than just a race; it's a pilgrimage for motorsport enthusiasts.
From the hairpin to the final corner, the fans are right on top of the action, creating an amphitheater of speed.
historicalReferences: Remember the 1966 Sebring 12 Hours? Ford's clean sweep was a defining moment in their battle with Ferrari.
The 1970 Sebring saw a dramatic finish with the Ferrari 512S winning by just seconds after a grueling race.
Who can forget Mario Andretti's dominant performance in the 1967 Sebring 12 Hours? A true masterclass of endurance racing.
The 1984 Sebring was a classic with the Porsche 935s battling it out in the Florida sun. A legendary era.
The 1993 IMSA GTP race was a barn burner, Juan Manuel Fangio II taking victory. A truly thrilling race.
The 2010 ALMS race saw a close finish between the Peugeot and Audi prototypes. A great battle of endurance.
The 2011 Sebring 12 hours, the debut of the Peugeot 908, a truly dominant machine that would set the standard for years to come.
In 2013, the Audi R18 e-tron quattro showed its dominance, proving that hybrid technology could win at Sebring.
The 2017 WEC race at Sebring saw a dramatic late-race safety car, shaking up the order and leading to a thrilling finish.
In 2019, the privateer Rebellion Racing team took a stunning victory, proving that David can beat Goliath at Sebring.

Negotiating the tricky Turn 10, the bridge, where the track narrows and punishes mistakes.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a major factor at Sebring, particularly on the softer compounds. Expect teams to closely monitor wear levels.
The long pit lane at Sebring adds significant time to each stop, making strategic decisions all the more critical.
Fuel consumption will be a key consideration, especially in the closing stages of the race. Can they make it to the end without another stop?
Traffic management is crucial on this tight and twisty circuit. A well-timed pit stop can gain valuable track position.
With the high likelihood of safety cars at Sebring, teams need to be ready to react quickly and adjust their strategy accordingly.
The bumpy surface takes its toll on the cars, increasing the risk of mechanical failures. Reliability is paramount.
A longer first stint might be beneficial to get ahead, but it will punish the tyres and require careful management from the driver.
The pit window here is around 30 seconds, a long time to lose on track, so strategic calls are very important.
weatherCommentary: The Florida humidity is relentless today, impacting both the drivers and the cars.
That cloud cover could bring a welcome respite from the heat, but it could also mean rain is on the way.
The wind is picking up across the circuit, making the already challenging conditions even more unpredictable.
The track temperature is soaring, pushing the tires to their limits and increasing the risk of blistering.
The chance of thunderstorms later in the race is looming large, potentially throwing the strategy out the window.
